extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, national authorities, judges, policymakers and stakeholders interested in the European/unitary patent litigation framework
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Agreement on a Unified Patent Court (UPCA) setting out the UPC's scope, structure, transitional arrangements, judges, applicable law, and competences for disputes concerning European patents and unitary patents across participating EU Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (which rights/acts are covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unified Patent Court Agreement (UPCA) applies to: European patents with unitary effect; supplementary protection certificates issued for products protected by a European patent; European patents without unitary effect; European patent applications that are pending on the date of application of this agreement or that are filed after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement is open for any Member State to join.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court structure (bodies and divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unified Patent Court (UPC) consists of a Court of First Instance (CFI), a Court of Appeal and a Registry. The CFI will have central, regional and local divisions. The central division will be based in Paris with a section in Munich (an additional section could be designated in the future). The Court of Appeal will be based in Luxembourg along with the Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFI's multi-level structure (central/regional/local) is intended to allocate cases geographically and by subject-matter; central division has specified seat(s) but further sections may be designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional period duration and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A 7-year transitional period will come into effect once the agreement has been applied. This may be extended for a further 7 years by a decision of the Administrative Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transitional period's fixed term and the Administrative Committee's power to extend it govern the temporary coexistence of national litigation and UPC jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional period effects on forum choice and opt-out
rubrics_metrics.description: During the transitional period: an action for infringement or for revocation of a European patent (but not for a European patent with unitary effect) may still be brought before a national court or other competent national authority; an action for infringement or for declaration of invalidity of a supplementary protection certificate, issued for a product protected by a European patent, may also be brought before a national court or other competent national authority; the holder of, or applicant for, a European patent or the holder of a supplementary protection certificate may opt out from the exclusive powers of the UPC, by notifying their opt-out to the Registry at the latest 1 month before the end of the transitional period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-out is time-limited (notification to Registry no later than one month before transitional period ends). During transition, national courts retain certain jurisdiction for non-unitary European patents and SPC matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges — appointment authority and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges are appointed by the Administrative Committee. Some judges will be legally qualified; others technically qualified. The pool of judges selected must include at least one technical judge for each field of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments must ensure both legal and technical expertise; the technical-judge-per-field requirement ensures technical capabilities for patent litigation across technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges — allocation, restrictions and allowable functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges will be allocated to divisions by the President of the CFI where required by the agreement or the related statute. No judge may hold any other occupation whether paid or unpaid. They may, however, hold judicial functions at national level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation can be made at the request of a local or regional division in cases such as counterclaims for revocation; strict prohibition on other occupations preserves independence while permitting national judicial roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of law to be applied by the UPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC will base its decisions on: EU law, including Regulations (EU) 1257/2012 and (EU) 1260/2012; the UPCA; the Convention on the Grant of European Patents (EPC); other international agreements applicable to patents and binding on all the participating Member States; and national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must integrate multiple legal sources (EU instruments, the UPCA itself, EPC, other international commitments, and relevant national law) in determining outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence / exclusive powers of the UPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC will have exclusive powers over a number of issues in the participating Member States, including actions for: actual or threatened infringements of European patents and supplementary protection certificates and related defences, including counterclaims concerning licences; provisional and protective measures and injunctions; revocation of European patents; and declaration of invalidity of supplementary protection certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UPC's exclusivity covers substantive infringement and validity disputes (and related provisional relief), centralising these aspects of patent litigation in participating states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force / provisional application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering the rules for entry into force of the UPCA (Article 89) and the ratifications made so far, the agreement will apply from the first day of the fourth month after Germany deposits its instrument of ratification with the Council of the European Union. Since 19 January 2022, certain rules of the UPCA already apply under the protocol on the provisional application of the UPCA; for instance, the UPC has legal personality and may recruit judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force is tied to specific ratification steps (Article 89) and some UPCA provisions can be provisionally applied before full entry into force, enabling preparatory measures (e.g., staffing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: SPCs issued for products protected by a European patent fall within the UPCA's scope; during the transitional period actions for infringement or for declaration of invalidity of an SPC may also be brought before national courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are explicitly included in both the UPC's substantive competence and the transitional arrangements allowing national-court actions for SPCs.
